# requireInteger

<link-summary>Returns the value as an integer, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireInteger() — Returns the value as an integer, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireInteger(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected an integer."): number;
```

A number with no fractional part. Nothing is coerced, so the string `"42"` is not an integer, and `NaN` is not either.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                         | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                           | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected an integer."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as an integer.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                    |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not an integer. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireInteger(42); // => 42
requireInteger(-7); // => -7
requireInteger(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireInteger(NaN); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
